subject.title: fix(browser): keep guarded CDP sockets on validated endpoints [AI]

question: Should the default Browser CDP policy continue supporting existing Chrome MCP profiles with explicit `cdpUrl`, or should OpenClaw intentionally fail them closed and require a driver/profile migration?
rationale: The implementation changes an established profile contract at a security boundary; code review cannot determine whether maintainers intend a default compatibility break or a narrower strict-mode restriction.

options.title: Preserve default Chrome MCP attachments
options.body: Keep explicit Chrome MCP `cdpUrl` attachments working under the default policy and apply the new transport restriction only when an explicitly selected guarded mode requires DNS pinning.

options.title: Adopt the fail-closed migration
options.body: Keep the rejection, but document the upgrade contract and provide a clear supported recovery or migration path for existing affected profiles.

recommendation.title: Preserve default Chrome MCP attachments
recommendation.body: Keep explicit Chrome MCP `cdpUrl` attachments working under the default policy and apply the new transport restriction only when an explicitly selected guarded mode requires DNS pinning.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans Browser CDP policy and Chrome MCP profile behavior.
